{{Conjecture|legends}}
{{Quote|The artist is humanoid, proportioned differently from humans and Chiss, with either a wider torso or longer arms. There's something of a distance to his emotional state, too. I would say his people are both drawn to and yet repulsed by or fearful of the physical objects they live among.|Thrawn, upon encountering Pashvi sculpture|<ref name="OF 8" />}}
'''This sculpture''' was created by [[Pashvi/Legends|Pashvi]] artistry. The sculpture was [[Color/Legends|blue and white]], and the design was elaborate. At some point by [[27 BBY/Legends|27 BBY]], the sculpture&mdash;and 12 others like it&mdash; had been stolen by [[Pirate/Legends|pirates]] of the [[Vagaari/Legends|Vagaari]] species. The artwork was placed in the hold of their [[Vagaari plunder ship|starship]]. Later, this vessel came under the control of the Chiss [[Commander/Legends|Commander]] [[Mitth'raw'nuruodo/Legends|Mitth'raw'nuruodo]]&mdash;also known as Thrawn. By analyzing this work of art, along its twelve mates, Thrawn surmised that the Pashvi were [[Humanoid/Legends|humanoid]] but proportioned differently from [[Human/Legends|Humans]] or Chiss, and that they had a distant emotional state. This reasoning impressed the [[Smuggler/Legends|smuggler]] [[Dubrak Qennto]], with whom Thrawn was traveling.<ref name="OF 8">[[Outbound Flight (novel)|''Outbound Flight'']], Chapter 8.</ref>
